1Outcome

Each participant receives supports that build the knowledge, skills and abilities of the family and other collaborating providers in order to support the child’s learning and development.

2Quality indicators

(1)

Work is undertaken with the support network in each child’s life to build their capacity to achieve the functional outcomes identified in the support plan.

Our commitment: Policy C1, Policy C2. Proof: Register col W.

(2)

Each family’s confidence is built to understand how their family routines and everyday activities can support their child’s development.

Our commitment: Policy C3, Policy C4, Policy C5. Proof: Register col W.

(3)

The capacity of the child, family and collaborating providers involved with the child is built through coaching, capacity building supports and collaborative teamwork.

Our commitment: Policy C3, Policy C6, Policy C7, Policy C13. Proof: Register col W.

(4)

Collaboration is undertaken to affirm, challenge, and support the child, family and collaborating providers to further develop their skills and to improve practice and relationships.

Our commitment: Policy C7, Policy C8, Policy C11.

(5)

Feedback and learnings from the child, family and other professionals is used to improve support delivery.

Our commitment: Policy C9, Policy C10, Policy C12, Policy C13. Proof: Register col X.

docs.html:
1Purpose

[Provider name] builds the skills and confidence of the family and others in a child's life, so the plan works between our visits. This policy is for families, our and the services we work with.

2Applies to

  • Every child who receives early childhood supports from us (the participant), and their family.
  • The other people in the child's life whom the family asks us to work with: carers, brothers and sisters (with a parent's agreement and a parent present), educators and other providers.
  • Every practitioner and manager of ours who coaches or plans . This covers employees, contractors, students and volunteers.
  • Every setting: the family home, early learning, school, the community, our premises, and phone or video.

This policy does not bind other providers. It sets how we work with them.

3Commitments

C1

We will coach at least one person from the child's for each the family is working on. We hold the first coaching session within 10 of the interim plan being agreed under POL-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Policy (Early Childhood Supports), or of the full plan being approved where there was no interim plan.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 1, Procedure step 5, Procedure step 6.

C2

We will ask the family, at the first session and at every , who else in the child's life should learn the strategies. We work with an educator or another provider only when the family has agreed and their consent covers what we share.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 3, Procedure step 19, Procedure step 23.

C3

We will coach inside the of the child's day. Each session starts from what the person wants to try. We watch the routine, help the person practise, reflect with them and agree what they will try next.

Answers: Legislation (2), Legislation (3). How we do it: Procedure step 2, Procedure step 5, Procedure step 8, Procedure step 9, Procedure step 11, Procedure step 12.

C4

We will build each family's confidence to see how everyday routines help their child learn. At the end of each coaching session we ask each person to rate, on a five point scale, how confident they feel to use the strategy for that outcome on their own this week, and we compare it with their last rating. We write down what they say in their own words.

Answers: Legislation (2). How we do it: Procedure step 7, Procedure step 17.

C5

We will change our approach when a person's confidence does not grow, and hand over when the child is progressing. If a person's rating has not risen over 3 sessions in a row, we ask what would help and change one thing within 10 business days. We space out sessions or move to the next outcome only when the rating is 4 or 5 in 3 sessions in a row and the child's latest progress check in FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan shows 'progressing' or 'achieved'. A change to an outcome goes to the progress check under PRO-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Procedure (Early Childhood Supports).

Answers: Legislation (2). How we do it: Procedure step 17, Procedure step 25, Procedure step 27.

C6

We will give each person a note of what they will try before our next contact, in the form they choose. We give it before we leave, or within 1 business day.

Answers: Legislation (3). How we do it: Procedure step 18.

C7

We will work as one team with other providers. Before a we agree with the other provider who leads each part, so the family hears one message.

Answers: Legislation (3), Legislation (4). How we do it: Procedure step 4, Procedure step 16.

C8

We will affirm what is working, invite each person to think about what they could do differently, and offer support, in every coaching session. We raise a concern about anyone's practice in private and with respect.

Answers: Legislation (4). How we do it: Procedure step 13, Procedure step 14, Procedure step 15.

C9

We will ask for feedback at the end of every session, from each person coached and from the child in the way the child communicates. We ask in full at least every 6 months. With the family's consent, we include educators and other providers in the team.

Answers: Legislation (5). How we do it: Procedure step 9, Procedure step 20, Procedure step 27.

C10

We will act on feedback. Where feedback asks for a change, or a rating fell, the decides what to change within 10 business days and tells the person what we changed, or why we did not, within 5 business days of the decision. Other feedback is read at the feedback review. A complaint goes to the complaints process the same day.

Answers: Legislation (5). How we do it: Procedure step 21, Procedure step 25, Procedure step 26.

C11

We will improve our own coaching. A practitioner coaches only after training in coaching, recorded in REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register. Each practitioner writes what they learned from sessions and brings it to . The 's quarterly read of each practitioner's records under POL-ECS-07 Evidence-Informed Practice Policy (Early Childhood Supports) covers 2 session records and agrees one change in coaching practice.

Answers: Legislation (4). How we do it: Procedure step 22, Procedure step 28, Procedure step 29.

C12

We will use what we learn from all families. Every 6 months the Quality Manager reads the feedback and ratings, raises improvements and reports to the governing body in the one early childhood quality report that covers sections 56 to 62.

Answers: Legislation (5). How we do it: Procedure step 30.

C13

We will write down each session the same day, in the words of the people who took part. We enter it in the register within 2 business days.

Answers: Legislation (3), Legislation (5). How we do it: Procedure step 22, Procedure step 24, Procedure step 29.

4Ground rules

G1

The family decides how their child's routines run. A person can say no to coaching, to being watched, to a rating, to filming or to anyone joining. Saying no never reduces supports.

G2

We build skill and do not take over. We show a strategy only when the person agrees, then hand it back.

G3

We coach only strategies that are in the child's plan, or that the family and the plan lead have agreed to add. Medicine and any health procedure are coached only by a practitioner qualified for it. A mealtime or swallowing strategy may be coached by the only when the qualified practitioner's written plan names what the key worker may coach, the practitioner has shown the key worker, and the practitioner reviews it at the interval the plan sets. This is role release, as POL-ECS-07 Evidence-Informed Practice Policy (Early Childhood Supports) sets.

G4

We never coach anyone to restrain, seclude or confine a child to manage behaviour. We tell the Service Manager the same day.

G5

A parent, carer or educator is present for the whole session. A worker is alone with a child, out of sight of another adult, only under a control written in FRM-CHS-02 Child Safety Risk Assessment.

G6

We film, photograph or record a child or family only with the family's written agreement, recorded at FRM-ECS-05 Coaching Session Record question 7. We never film another child.

G7

We share information about a child only as the family's consent in FRM-ECS-04 Team Around the Child Record allows.

G8

A concern that a child is at risk of harm comes before coaching. It follows PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports).

How we do it: Procedure step 10.

G9

A concern about how a colleague practises goes to the Practice supervisor. A concern about a colleague's conduct towards a child or family, or about safety, goes to the Chief Executive; a concern about the Chief Executive goes to the chair of the governing body. A sole trader's concern goes to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. A concern that a child is at risk of harm goes to the the same day, under PRO-ECS-02. This is the one rule POL-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Policy sets for every early childhood document.

G10

Each fact is held once. REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register holds dates, people coached, ratings and short feedback entries. FRM-ECS-05 Coaching Session Record holds the detail.

5Who is responsible

Governing bodyReading the 6 monthly report on feedback and ratings. Resourcing supervision and time with families

PractitionerRuns each session. Checks consent first. Records the session the same day. Writes what they learned
Practice supervisorReads each practitioner's records every 3 months in the one quarterly read under POL-ECS-07, including 2 session records, and agrees one change in coaching practice. In a small provider this is one outside clinical supervisor with early childhood experience
Quality ManagerReads the feedback and ratings across all children every 6 months. Raises improvements. Reports to the governing body
Independent contact for concernsIn a sole trader's business, receives concerns about the sole trader and reads a sample of 3 session records every 6 months

In a small provider one person may hold several of these roles. A sole trader holds all of them except the Practice supervisor, the independent contact and the governing body. A sole trader engages one outside clinical supervisor as Practice supervisor, whose quarterly read covers coaching, practice and plans together, and one independent contact. POL-ECS-07 says how a sole trader may source them.

The checks in this table are run as three events, not as separate readings: the monthly REG-ECS-01 check (owned by REG-ECS-01 'How we review'), the Practice supervisor's quarterly read of each practitioner's records and plans together (POL-ECS-07), and the 6 monthly early childhood quality report to the governing body covering sections 56 to 62.

helping a parent, carer, educator or other provider practise a strategy in the child's own routine, in place of doing it for them.
capacity building support
any support other than a coaching visit that builds the skill or knowledge of a person in the child's life. It can be a demonstration, a short training for educators, a picture guide or a shared video.

the relatives, friends, educators and providers in the child's everyday life whom the family chooses to involve.

something the child does most days, such as a meal, bath time, play, getting dressed, a trip, or group time at early learning.

something the child will do in daily life, written in the plan so the family can see when it has happened.

how confident a person says they feel, at the end of a session, to use the strategy for an outcome on their own this week, from 1 (not at all) to 5 (very).

the practitioner accountable for the child's plan and the register row.

the one practitioner the family chooses as their main contact. Where the family chooses a key worker of ours, that person is the plan lead.

the worker of ours who runs a coaching session.
Practice supervisor
the clinical supervisor of the early childhood practitioners, who gives each practitioner reflective supervision and reads their records.

a session in which the plan lead asks each person how useful the coaching is and how working together is going.
child safety lead
the role the Chief Executive names to receive every concern about a child and to see that reports are made.

a meeting in which a practitioner and the Practice supervisor look at the practitioner's own work and learn from it.

a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

docs.html:
1Purpose

The result: each person in the child's life leaves every session more able and confident to help the child reach the plan's outcomes. The family comes first. What they tell us changes how we work.

This procedure gives effect to POL-ECS-06 Capacity Building Policy (Early Childhood Supports), C1 to C13.

2When and who

Start this procedure when the family agrees the interim plan under PRO-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Procedure (Early Childhood Supports), within 10 of the first session, and again when the full plan, FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan, is approved. Then follow it for every session, , and . A session can be at home, at early learning, at school, in the community, at our premises or by phone or video.

Who acts:

  • The books the first session, enters sessions in the register and holds the feedback review. The plan lead also decides what to change and tells people (steps 1 and 24 to 27).
  • The runs each session and records it (steps 2 to 23).
  • The reads session records and agrees one change with each practitioner (step 28).
  • The Service Manager checks the register every month (step 29).
  • The Quality Manager reads the feedback and ratings across all children every 6 months (step 30).

In a small provider one person may hold several of these roles. A sole trader is the plan lead, the practitioner and the Service Manager. A sole trader engages one outside clinical supervisor with early childhood experience as the Practice supervisor, whose quarterly read covers coaching, practice and plans together. A sole trader also asks the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register to read 3 session records every 6 months.

3Before you start

  • The family has agreed the interim plan, or the full plan is approved. You have read its outcomes and the it names.
  • You have read the team record, FRM-ECS-04 Team Around the Child Record. You know who is in the team and what the family agreed may be shared.
  • Your worker screening clearance and your working with children check are current in REG-HRM-01 Worker Screening Register. You have signed FRM-CHS-01 Child Safe Code of Conduct and Acknowledgement.
  • You have the last FRM-ECS-05 Coaching Session Record for this child and the last note you gave.
  • You have a blank FRM-ECS-05. It holds the confidence scale.
  • You are trained to coach, and the training is recorded in REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register.
  • An interpreter is booked if the family wants one.
  • For a phone or video session, a parent, carer or educator is with the child.

4Watch out

  • A worker alone with a child. A worker out of sight of a parent, carer or educator puts the child at risk. It also exposes the worker to a false claim.
  • Sharing without consent. Telling an educator or another provider about the child without the family's agreement breaks trust. It can also breach the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).
  • Filming. A recording of a child, or of another child in the room, without written agreement is a privacy breach and a child safety risk.
  • Taking over. If you do the strategy for the person every time, they do not learn it. The child's progress stops when you leave.
  • Rating for the person. Your own view in the person's rating box hides what they told you. The register then shows progress that is not real.
  • A strategy outside your scope. Coaching eating, drinking or swallowing without the qualified practitioner's written release, or medicine or any health procedure without the right qualification, can seriously hurt a child.
  • A strategy that restrains a child. Coaching anyone to restrain, seclude or confine a child can cause harm and breach the child's rights.
  • Challenge in public. Questioning a person's practice in front of the child, another family or their colleagues shames them and ends the working relationship.
  • Feedback that is a complaint. A complaint left in a session record can sit unanswered. The person may stop telling us anything.

5Steps

Set up

Step 1

Plan lead

Book the first coaching session.

Choose a time in a routine the plan names. Ask the family for the place, the language and any help they need to take part. Book an interpreter if they want one. Coaching starts under the interim plan; the full plan replaces it (PRO-ECS-08 Decision table 4).

Result
The first session is booked, in the family's own routine.
Record
None
Time limit
The session is held within 10 business days of the interim plan being agreed, or of the full plan being approved where there was no interim plan (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C1.

Before each session

Step 2

Practitioner

Agree the session with each person.

Say what you plan to do and why. Ask each person where and when suits, how they like to learn, and what help they need to take part. For an educator, agree the visit with the service leader first. Tell an educator or another provider that the family can read what they say.

Result
Each person knows what to expect and has chosen how they learn.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q6 and Q11
Time limit
Before the session (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C3. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q6, FRM-ECS-05 Q11.

Step 3

Practitioner

Check what the family has agreed about sharing and recording.

For each person outside the family, open FRM-ECS-04 Q7, Q8 and Q12. Confirm that a consent line covers that person, what you will say and the purpose, and that it has not been changed or withdrawn. If it does not, do not contact them: ask the family. For any filming, photographing or recording, look for the family's written agreement recorded at FRM-ECS-05 Q7 for this session or an earlier one. Never record another child. If everyone is family and nothing will be recorded, write "family only" and "no".

Result
You share and record only what the family agreed.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q5 and Q7
Time limit
Before you contact anyone outside the family, and again at the start of the session (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C2. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q5, FRM-ECS-05 Q7.

Step 4

Practitioner

If another provider will take part:

Agree with the other provider who leads each part.

Do this before the session, and only after step 3. Agree what each of you will say to the family, so they hear one message. If your advice differs, settle it between you first, away from the family and the child.

Result
One plan and one message for the family.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q4
Time limit
Before the session (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C7. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q4.

In the session

Step 5

Practitioner

Ask each person what they want to try or understand today.

Start from their words. Link their answer to an outcome in the plan and to a routine the child really has. Write the outcome and the routine as the plan states them.

Result
The focus belongs to the person and is tied to the plan.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q8, Q9 and Q10
Time limit
At the start of the session (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C1, Policy C3. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q8, FRM-ECS-05 Q9, FRM-ECS-05 Q10.

Step 6

Practitioner

If the person wants to work on something that is not an outcome in the plan:

Tell the plan lead the same day.

Today, coach on an outcome that is in the plan. Write "not in the plan" at Q8. The plan lead starts a plan review as Decision table 2 sets out.

Result
The plan lead knows the plan does not fit, and the plan review starts. Coaching does not drift away from the plan.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q8
Time limit
The same day (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C1. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q8.

Step 7

Practitioner

Recall the last rating for this outcome and ask what has changed since.

Read back the end rating from the last session record for this outcome (FRM-ECS-05 Q17). Ask what the person has tried since and how it went. Write their words. Do not ask for a new rating now: the one rating for the session is taken at step 17.

Result
The person's starting point for today is their last rating, in their own words.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q18
Time limit
At the start of the session (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C4. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q17.

Step 8

Practitioner

If the person says no to any part of the session:

Stop that part.

Say that no never reduces supports. Ask whether another time, place, way or person would suit. Write what they declined and what you did instead.

Result
The person's choice is respected and the session goes on in a way they accept.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q24
Time limit
At once (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C3. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q24.

Step 9

Warning. A worker alone with a child, out of sight of a parent, carer or educator, puts the child at risk.

Practitioner

Watch the person and the child in the routine.

Let the person do it their usual way first. A parent, carer or educator stays in the room. Write what each person does and how the child takes part. Notice how the child shows what they like and dislike.

Result
You have facts about what is working, and the child's own response.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q13 and Q15
Time limit
During the session (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C3, Policy C9. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q13, FRM-ECS-05 Q15.

Step 10

Practitioner

If the child is hurt or unwell, or you see or hear anything that worries you about the child's safety:

Stop coaching and keep the child safe.

Call 000 if there is immediate danger. For an injury, follow WIN-INC-01 Responding to an Incident (frontline). For a concern about harm, follow PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) and tell the the same day. Never promise a child you will keep a secret. Do not wait to finish the session.

Result
The child is safe and the right person knows.
Record
FRM-INC-01 for an injury, or FRM-ECS-01 for a concern about harm
Time limit
Straight away (our standard)

Carries out: Policy G8. Written on: FRM-ECS-01.

Step 11

Practitioner

Help each person try the strategy in the routine.

Use the least help that works. First let the person lead, and give feedback. Then do it together. Show how only if the person agrees, then hand it back. Offer a picture, written or video guide if it helps. Coach only strategies in the plan, and use Decision table 2 for any that you cannot coach.

Result
The person has practised the strategy, with support, in the real routine.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q14
Time limit
During the session (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C3. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q14.

Step 12

Practitioner

Ask each person what they noticed.

Ask what they saw the child do, and what it tells them about how this routine helps the child learn. Write their words, not yours.

Result
The person says, in their own words, how the routine supports the child's development.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q16
Time limit
Straight after the practice (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C3. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q16.

Step 13

Practitioner

Affirm what is working.

Name exactly what the person did and how the child responded. Say it to the person, not about them. Tell the child too, in a way they understand.

Result
The person knows what to keep doing.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q20
Time limit
During the session (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C8. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q20.

Step 14

Practitioner

Ask each person to think about one thing they could do differently.

Ask a question, not a verdict. For example, ask what might happen if they tried it another way. Ask in private, not in front of the child, another family or the person's colleagues. If the person's way could harm the child or goes against the plan, use Decision table 2.

Result
The person has thought about a change and chosen what to do about it.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q21
Time limit
During the session (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C8. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q21.

Step 15

Practitioner

Offer support.

Support can be another visit, a call, a guide, a joint session with another provider or a team meeting. Agree with the person what you will do and by when.

Result
The person knows what help they can count on.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q22
Time limit
During the session (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C8. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q22.

Step 16

Practitioner

If two people disagree about how to support the child:

Ask the family to decide.

First hear each view and write it down. The family decides how their child's routines run, unless the strategy puts the child at risk (step 10). If the disagreement is between services, bring it to the next team meeting under PRO-ECS-05 Collaboration Procedure (Early Childhood Supports).

Result
One agreed way, or a team meeting booked.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q23
Time limit
During the session (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C7. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q23.

Step 17

Practitioner

Ask each person to rate their confidence again.

Use the scale on the form: 1 is not confident at all and 5 is very confident. Offer five faces or a count on one hand if the person prefers. The person chooses the number. Write what they say. A person may choose not to rate: write that. Compare with the last rating for this outcome at Q18. If the rating has not risen, ask what would help. If this is the third session in a row with no rise, tell the plan lead the same day.

Result
The end rating is in the person's own words.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q17, Q18 and Q19
Time limit
At the end of the session (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C4, Policy C5. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q18, FRM-ECS-05 Q19.

End of the session

Step 18

Practitioner

Write each person a note of what they will try before next time.

Agree it with them first: one or two things, the routine, the day, and how we will hear how it went. Write the note in the form the person chose: print, large print, pictures, audio, video, message or translated.

Result
Each person holds a note they can use.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q25 and Q26
Time limit
Before you leave, or within 1 business day (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C6. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q25, FRM-ECS-05 Q26.

Step 19

Practitioner

If this is the first session, or a feedback review:

Ask who else in the child's life could help with this outcome.

Ask about grandparents, other carers, brothers and sisters, the early learning service and other providers. The family decides. If they say yes, add the person to the team at FRM-ECS-04 Q4 and give them a consent line at Q7 before you contact them.

Result
The is as wide as the family wants it.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q12
Time limit
During the session (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C2. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q12.

Step 20

Practitioner

Ask each person what they thought of the session.

Ask: "What was most useful? What would you change?" Write their words. Ask an educator or another provider only if their consent line at FRM-ECS-04 Q7 allows it. Read back each person's own words from the session and ask whether they are right. Then thank them.

Result
You have each person's feedback in their own words.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q28
Time limit
At the end of the session (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C9. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q28.

Step 21

Practitioner

If anyone says they are unhappy with something:

Pass it to the complaints process.

Treat it as a complaint however the person says it. Follow PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. Do not try to settle it yourself. Tell the person what happens next. Nobody is treated worse for complaining.

Result
The complaint is in REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register, and the person knows what happens next.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q29
Time limit
The same day (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C10. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q29.

After the session

Step 22

Practitioner

Complete the session record.

Answer every question that applies, in the words of the people who took part. At Q30 write one thing to keep doing and one thing to do differently. Bring Q30 to your next under PRO-ECS-07 Evidence-Informed Practice Procedure (Early Childhood Supports).

Result
A full, signed record of the session is in the child's file.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 and Q30
Time limit
The same day (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C11, Policy C13. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q1, FRM-ECS-05 Q2, FRM-ECS-05 Q3, FRM-ECS-05 Q4, FRM-ECS-05 Q30.

Step 23

Practitioner

If you shared anything from the session with anyone outside the family:

Log the exchange: a line for a document or a new person, or the consent line used in the progress note.

Check the family's consent first. For a report or document sent, or the first exchange with a new person, write the date, what you shared, from whom, to whom, how and your name at FRM-ECS-04 Q29, and the date of that line at Q27. For a routine call or email within an existing consent line, write "consent checked: Q7 line N" at Q27 instead.

Result
Every exchange outside the family is within consent, and is on the log or names its consent line.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q27; FRM-ECS-04 Q29
Time limit
The same day (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C2. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q27, FRM-ECS-04 Q29.

Step 24

Plan lead, from the signed FRM-ECS-05

Enter the session in the register.

In REG-ECS-01 column W, enter the date and the number of records this plan period. Enter who was coached, by role, and the parent's or carer's end rating. In column X, enter who gave feedback, what they said in short, and the REG-FBK-01 reference if anyone was unhappy. Enter how the child responded in column AH (the child's own views). Leave "what we changed" for step 25.

Result
The register shows the session and the feedback.
Record
REG-ECS-01 col W; REG-ECS-01 col X
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the session (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C13. Written on: Register col W, Register col X.

Learn and improve

Step 25

Plan lead

Decide what to change because of the feedback and what you learned.

Read Q19 and Q28 to Q30. Decide where the feedback asks for a change or a rating fell; carry other feedback to the feedback review at step 27. Use Decision table 1 where ratings did not rise or stayed high. A change for this family goes into the plan, FRM-ECS-07, with them. A change that could help other families goes into REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register, using FRM-QMS-01 Improvement / Corrective Action Request Form. Write each decision at Q31 and add it to REG-ECS-01 column X with the REG-QMS-01 entry number.

Result
Every piece of feedback has a decision, with a reason if the decision is no change.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q31; REG-ECS-01 col X
Time limit
Within 10 business days of the session (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C5, Policy C10. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q31, Register col X.

Step 26

Plan lead

Tell each person what we changed, or why we did not.

Tell the person who gave the feedback, in the form they chose. If the feedback came from a child, tell the parent or carer and show the child in their own way.

Result
Each person who gave feedback knows what happened to it.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q32
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the decision (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C10. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q32.

Step 27

Plan lead

Hold the feedback review with the family.

Hold it at least every 6 months, at every plan review and whenever a person asks. Ask each person on their own how useful the coaching is and what they would change. Ask how working together is going between us and each other provider, with the family's consent. Read the ratings across the records for this plan period, and use Decision table 1. Agree any change with the family.

Result
The family and the team have had their say on the coaching as a whole.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q33, Q34 and Q35
Time limit
At least every 6 months (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C5, Policy C9. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q33, FRM-ECS-05 Q34, FRM-ECS-05 Q35.

Check

Step 28

Practice supervisor

Read 2 session records for each practitioner, as part of the quarterly read.

This is part of the one quarterly read of each practitioner's records and plans under PRO-ECS-07 Evidence-Informed Practice Procedure (Early Childhood Supports). Pick one session record at random and one the practitioner chooses. Check that each shows an outcome, a routine, each person's own words, the rating and how it compares with the last session, a next step and feedback. Check whether the practitioner affirmed, asked and offered support, and whether the person did more of the work each time. Agree one change with the practitioner. Write what you found at Q36 and Q37.

Result
A second reader has checked each practitioner's coaching, and each practitioner has one change to try.
Record
FRM-ECS-05 Q36 and Q37
Time limit
Every 3 months (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C11. Written on: FRM-ECS-05 Q36, FRM-ECS-05 Q37.

Step 29

Service Manager

Check the coaching entries in the register.

This is the monthly REG-ECS-01 check under REG-ECS-01 'How we review'; one check covers sections 56 to 62. Read column W and column X for every child with a current plan. Flag any child with no coaching record in the last 3 months. Flag a first session more than 10 business days after the interim plan was agreed or the plan approved (column S). Flag a late entry. Flag 3 sessions in a row with no rise in rating and no change at Q31. Flag a document shared at Q27 with no line in FRM-ECS-04 Q29. Flag feedback that asked for a change with no decision after 10 business days. Check that each practitioner who ran a session has a coaching entry in REG-HRM-02. Read 3 session records in full. Give each gap an owner and a date.

Result
Gaps are found within a month and each has an owner.
Record
REG-ECS-01 col AK
Time limit
Every month. Each gap is fixed within 5 business days (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C11, Policy C13. Written on: Register col AE.

Step 30

Quality Manager

Report what the feedback and ratings across all children show.

Read them first. Group the feedback in REG-ECS-01 column X by theme. Count the ratings that rose, stayed the same and fell. Count the complaints, and count the practice changes agreed at Q37. Raise each theme that touches more than one family in REG-QMS-01. Include it in the 6 monthly early childhood quality report to the governing body that covers sections 56 to 62.

Result
What we learn from all families is used to improve how we deliver supports.
Record
REG-QMS-01
Time limit
Every 6 months (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C12.

6Decision

Decision table 1: What the ratings and the person's words tell us

IfThenWhoBy when
The rating has not risen over 3 sessions in a row for the same outcomeAsk what would help (Q19). Change one thing: the routine, the place, the method, the length of the session or the practitioner. Try it for 2 sessions, then look againPlan lead, with the personWithin 10 business days of the third session (our standard)
The rating is 4 or 5 in 3 sessions in a row, the person does the strategy on their own, and the latest progress check in FRM-ECS-07 Q30 says 'progressing' or 'achieved'Agree to space out the sessions or move to the next outcome. Tell the person their skill has grown. Take any change to the outcome to the progress check under PRO-ECS-08 step 23Plan lead, with the personAt the next session (our standard)
The rating is 4 or 5 in 3 sessions in a row, but the latest progress check in FRM-ECS-07 Q30 says 'no change' or 'gone back'Keep the sessions. Ask the plan lead to look at the strategy with the family at the progress check under PRO-ECS-08 step 23Practitioner, then plan leadAt the next progress check (our standard)
The end rating fell in one sessionAsk what happened. Ask whether the strategy did not fit or the person is under strain. Offer a call or a visitPractitionerAt the next contact, within 5 business days (our standard)
The person chooses not to rateWrite "chose not to rate" and use their words. Do not press. Ask again at the next feedback reviewPractitionerAt each session (our standard)
The person says coaching does not suit them, cancels 3 times in a row or stops answeringRing them and ask what would suit. Offer another way: a guide, a call, another time or another person. Tell them supports continue. Write the decision at the next plan reviewPlan leadWithin 5 business days of the third cancellation (our standard)

Decision table 2: When a strategy or request is not one you can coach

IfThenWhoBy when
The strategy is in the plan and within your qualification, or the qualified practitioner has released it to you in writingCoach itPractitionerDuring the session (our standard)
The person wants to work on something that is not an outcome in the plan, or the plan is out of dateCoach an outcome that is in the plan. Tell the plan lead. The plan lead starts a plan review under PRO-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Procedure (Early Childhood Supports)Practitioner, then plan leadPlan lead told the same day. Plan review started within 5 business days and held within 10 (our standard)
The strategy changes how the child eats, drinks or swallows, or it is a medicine or any other health procedureFor medicine or a health procedure, do not coach it unless you are qualified for it. For eating, drinking or swallowing, coach it only if you are qualified for it, or the qualified practitioner's written plan names what you may coach, they have shown you, and they review it at the set interval. Otherwise ask the plan lead to bring in a qualified health practitioner. Keep to the approach already in the plan until thenPractitioner, then plan leadPlan lead acts within 5 business days (our standard)
The strategy would restrain, seclude or confine the child to manage behaviourDo not coach it. Tell the Service Manager. Ask the family whether they want help from a behaviour support practitionerPractitioner, then Service ManagerThe same day (our standard)
The strategy puts the child at risk of harmStop and follow step 10PractitionerStraight away (our standard)
Two people disagree about a strategyFollow step 16PractitionerDuring the session (our standard)

7If it goes wrong

  • You cannot attend a session. Tell the Service Manager the day you know. The Service Manager follows the continuity arrangement the family agreed, in REG-ECS-01 column Y. That means sending a practitioner the child knows, or offering another time. The Service Manager tells the family the same day. The replacement reads the last record and the last note first.
  • An interpreter does not come, or a person cannot follow. Stop the parts that need words. Do not use the child, a brother or a sister to interpret. Rebook with an interpreter within 5 business days (our standard) and tell the family.
  • An educator's service will not allow the visit. Coach the family instead. Ask the family whether they agree to us giving the service a written summary. Tell the plan lead the same day. Raise it at the next team meeting.
  • The plan is out of date or does not name the outcome the family now wants. Use Decision table 2. Coaching continues only on outcomes in the plan until the plan review is done.
  • A deadline will be missed. Tell the Service Manager before the date, not after it. Write the reason and the new date in REG-ECS-01 column AK, and tell the family the new date. Never change a date on a record to hide a late one.
  • You are worried about how a colleague coaches. Tell the Practice supervisor. If you are worried about a colleague's conduct towards a child or family, or about safety, tell the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive, tell the chair of the governing body. A sole trader's concern goes to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01. This is the one rule POL-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Policy sets. A safety concern about a child never waits for this chain: follow step 10.
  • A recording was made without written agreement. Tell the Service Manager the same day. The Service Manager enters it in REG-INF-01 Data Breach Register, quarantines the recording, asks the family what they want done with it, and deletes it unless it must be kept as an incident or complaint record.
  • The system is down. Complete a paper FRM-ECS-05 the same day. Enter the session in the register within 1 business day of the system coming back.

8Done means

  • The session record is complete, signed and in the child's file the same day.
  • Each person has a note of what they will try, in the form they chose.
  • REG-ECS-01 columns W and X show the session, who was coached, the end rating and the feedback.
  • Any document shared outside the family is on the sharing log in FRM-ECS-04, and any routine exchange names its consent line.
  • Any complaint is in REG-FBK-01, and the person knows what happens next.
  • Each piece of feedback has a decision, and the person who gave it has been told.
  • After a feedback review, Section H is complete and any change is agreed with the family.

9Quick card

125 words
  • Keep a parent, carer or educator in the room. Never be alone with the child out of sight (step 9).
  • If a child is hurt or at risk, stop and act straight away (step 10).
  • Check what the family agreed before you share or film (step 3).
  • Start from what the person wants to try (step 5).
  • Ask for the at the end of the session, in the person's own words, and compare it with last time (step 17).
  • Affirm what is working, then ask, then offer support (step 13).
  • Write each person a note of what they will try (step 18).
  • Pass any unhappiness to the complaints process the same day (step 21).
  • Write the session record the same day (step 22).

questions.text: Which child is this about?
questions.hint: Give their full name, the name they like to be called and their date of birth. questions.section: Section A: The concern (worker)
questions.text: What is the incident report number, or is this not an incident?
questions.hint: Where the harm is connected with our supports or one of our workers, take the number from question 19 of FRM-INC-01 when the Quality Manager gives it, and write "not yet given" until then. Where it is not connected with our supports, write "not an incident: not connected with our supports". The child safety lead completes this.

questions.section: Section A: The concern (worker)
questions.text: What kind of concern is it?
questions.hint: Choose every kind that worries you. You do not need proof. "Harm connected with our supports or one of our workers" makes the concern an incident as well.

options: harm connected with our supports or one of our workers

questions.text: Why do you suspect the child is at risk of harm?
questions.hint: Where the concern is not an incident, this is the full account: what happened, in order, facts only; the child's exact words; the time; who else was there. questions.text: Who is the concern about?

one of our workers, managers or owners

form.intro:
Use this record for every concern that a child is at risk of harm, from anyone, in any place. It shows why we suspect, on reasonable grounds, that the child is at risk. It shows the report made to the child protection authority of [state or territory], and what happened next.

  • Section A: the who has the concern completes this the same day.
  • Section B: the child safety lead completes this during the worker's first call.
  • Section C: the person who made the report to the authority completes this. That is the worker, or the child safety lead.
  • Sections D and E: the child safety lead completes these as the concern is managed.

This record sits beside the incident report only where the harm is connected with the provision of our supports or with one of our workers (PRO-ECS-02 Decision table 2). In that case the worker's account of what happened goes on FRM-INC-01 Incident Report Form, as for any incident, and question 4 here is a short reason only. Where the concern is not connected with our supports, there is no incident report and no NDIS Commission notice: question 4 carries the full account.

Phone the child safety lead before you start writing. If a child is in danger, call 000 first.

Have ready: the child's name, date of birth and address, and the names of the people who live with them. Have the reference number the authority gave you.

What happens next: the child safety lead gives this record a number and enters it in REG-ECS-01 col J. PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets every step. When systems are down, use the paper copy kept at [location at each site].
form.privacy:
We collect this information to keep a child safe and to make reports under child protection law. We also collect it to meet our duties under the NDIS Act 2013.

Only the child safety lead, the deputy and the Chief Executive read it. The Quality Manager and auditors read REG-INC-01 and REG-ECS-01 col J, not this form. The and the Service Manager receive only the outcome for the child's supports and plan (questions 14 and 18), by note. We give parts of it to the child protection authority, police, the NDIS Commission and other bodies. We do this when the law requires or allows it. A report to the authority needs no consent.

A person with parental responsibility can ask what we hold about their child. We may hold back parts if giving them could put the child at risk. We also hold back parts if the law or an authority tells us not to. We remove other people's details first. We never tell the person a concern is about who raised it. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect this record.
form.after:
• Practitioner: phone the child safety lead first. Give Section A to the child safety lead, and to nobody else, the same day (our standard).
  • If the concern is about the child safety lead, give it to the deputy. If it is about the deputy, give it to the lead. If it is about a manager, give it to the lead and the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive or an owner, give it to the chair of the governing body. In a sole trader's business, give it to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register.
  • You can also report straight to the child protection authority or the NDIS Commission. POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy sets out how you are protected.
  • Child safety lead: complete Section B within 1 hour of the worker's call (our standard).
  • Child safety lead: give the record its number and enter it in REG-ECS-01 col J the same day (our standard).
  • Child safety lead: complete Section D within 1 of the concern (our standard).
  • Child safety lead: add dated entries to Section E until the record is closed. Read every open record at least every 20 business days (our standard).
  • Keep the closed record in the restricted section of the child's file. Keep it for 45 years from the day it is made (Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, recommendation 8.1; check the records law of [state or territory] at adoption). Where the concern is also an incident, the Incident Rules, section 12(4), minimum of 7 years applies as well. REG-ECS-01 sets the same period for the row where col J holds this record's number.

form.intro:
This is the team record for one child. It names the team around the child and the key worker if the family chose one. It records what the family agreed may be shared, each team meeting and each planned move.

Keep one team record for each child. It stays open while we support the child. Add dated entries. Never write over an old entry.

Who completes it:

  • The Service Manager completes question 1, question 3 and question 41.
  • The plan lead completes the rest of Sections A to D, and Sections G and H, with the family.
  • The plan lead adds one entry to Section E for each team meeting. A key worker of ours may do it with them.
  • Every practitioner of ours adds a line to Section F each time they send or receive a document, or share with a new person.

Have these ready:

  • the child's row in REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register
  • the family's communication preferences, on FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form
  • nothing else for consent: Section C of this record is the family's consent record for sharing within the team
  • any court order or agency letter about who decides for the child
  • the child's plan, FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan, once it is written.

PRO-ECS-05 Collaboration Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets every step. The family receives a copy of Sections A to C, of questions 13 to 15 and 17 to 20, and of every meeting entry. Question 16 stays in the file.

Do not write a child protection concern in this record. Use FRM-ECS-01 Child Protection Concern and Report Record. If you do not know an answer, write "not yet asked" and the date. Ask at the next contact with the family.
form.privacy:
This statement is for the family.

We collect this information so the people who support your child can work as one team. The NDIS Practice Standards require us to coordinate that team and to share information only with your consent.

form.intro:
This is the coaching session record. It records one session in which we build the skills and confidence of a person in the child's life. It shows what the person practised in the child's routine, what they will try next, how confident they feel and what they told us.

Complete one record for each session. Question 3 sets the kind of session: coaching, joint session with another provider, capacity building support or feedback review.

When | Complete these questions

Coaching session or joint session: questions 1 to 5, 7 to 9, 14, 16 to 18 and 24 to 28 are the minimum set (24 and 27 only when they apply). Complete the rest of Sections A to G when something relevant happened or when the asks.

Capacity building support only (a guide, a video, a short training): questions 1 to 5, 7, 8, 10 and 25 to 28.

First session or feedback review: the minimum set, plus questions 12 and 19 to 23 as they apply.

Six-monthly feedback review (plan lead): Section H.

Practice supervisor's quarterly read: Section I.

Question 1 is answered once per page where several sessions for one child are recorded on one day.

Who completes it:

  • The practitioner who ran the session completes the minimum question set the same day, and the rest of Sections A to G where relevant.
  • The plan lead completes Section H at least every 6 months, at every plan review and whenever a person asks.
  • The Practice supervisor completes Section I for each record they read.

Have ready:

  • the child's plan, FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan, for the outcomes and the routines
  • the team record, FRM-ECS-04 Team Around the Child Record, for who may take part and what may be shared
  • the last coaching session record for this child, and the last note you gave
  • the family's communication preferences, on FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form.

Write the words of the people who took part, as they said, signed or showed them. This form is not a test of any person and it has no pass mark.

What happens next: the dates, the people coached, the ratings and the feedback go to REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register within 2 business days. Where feedback asks for a change or a rating fell, the plan lead decides what to change within 10 business days; other feedback goes to the feedback review. PRO-ECS-06 Capacity Building Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets every step.
form.privacy:
Say this to the family before the first session, in the language and way they use:

"We write a record after each session. It helps us build on what you have tried, and it lets you see what we did and what you told us. We write down what you, your child, an educator or another provider say in the session, in your words where we can.

The practitioners who work with your child read this record. So do the Service Manager, the Practice supervisor and the Quality Manager when they check our work. We share it with an educator or another service only as you agreed in the team record.

You choose how far you take part. You can say no to being watched, to giving a rating, to anyone joining, or to coaching at all. Your child's supports continue either way.

We do not film, photograph or record your child unless you agree in writing first. We never film other children.

There is one exception to keeping your information private. The law may require us to share information without your consent to keep a child safe. PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets whether and when we tell you, following the advice of the child protection agency of [state or territory].

You can read this record, ask us to correct it and tell us if you are unhappy with anything. Ask [privacy contact role and contact details]."

Tell an educator or another provider that the family can read what they say.

[Provider name] handles this record under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy.

columns.meaning: The one number that follows this child through every early childhood record

columns.trail: Filled from: FRM-ECS-05 Q1.

columns.name: Family and support network

register.proves:
This register holds one row for every child who receives early childhood supports from [Provider name]. The row is the index to the child's file. It shows who the family is, who is in the team, what the family agreed to, and when each plan, review and report was due and done.

  • Indicators evidenced: s 56 (1) to s 56 (4), s 56 (5)(a) and s 56 (5)(b).
  • Also s 57 (1) to s 57 (8), on the family.
  • Also s 58 (1) to s 58 (4), on inclusion, and s 59 (1) to s 59 (4), on collaboration.
  • Also s 60 (1) to s 60 (5), on capacity building, and s 61 (2), on skills.
  • Also s 62 (1) to s 62 (6), on outcomes.
  • Legal basis: National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018, Schedule 5, clauses 3 to 9. Section 20(3), item 18 of those Rules applies Schedules 1 and 5 to early intervention supports for early childhood.
  • No NDIS instrument sets the columns of this register. The columns are our standard, built from the indicators.
  • Each fact is held once. The forms hold the detail and the family's words. This register holds the dates, the names, the counts, the record numbers and a one-line pointer to the form.
  • Clearances and training are in REG-HRM-01 Worker Screening Register and REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register. Intake and the service agreement are in REG-SUP-01 Participant and Service Agreement Register (Rise version not yet written); until it exists, column F holds who has parental responsibility.
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years after supports end, or until the child turns 25, whichever is later (our standard; NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years).
  • Retention where column J holds a record number: keep the row for 45 years (Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, recommendation 8.1; our standard). Check the child safe and records law of [state or territory] at adoption and before any row is destroyed.

Columns A to G and I are filled before the first session, and columns H and Y by the end of it. Column J stays blank until a record exists. Columns K to X and AH are filled as the plan is made and followed. Columns Z, AA and AD are filled when an interruption, a transition or an exit comes up. Columns AB, AC, AE, AF, AG, AI, AJ, AK and AL are kept current for every row.
register.entry:
1. The opens the row within 2 of the family accepting our offer (our standard). The Service Manager names the plan lead that day.
  2. Use one row for each child. Brothers and sisters each get their own row, linked in column AF.
  3. Fill columns A to G and I before the first session. Column J stays blank until a record exists. The first session does not go ahead while column I is empty for the type of setting it is in.
  4. Fill columns H and Y by the end of the first session.
  5. Fill every other column within 2 business days of the form or meeting that produces it (our standard).
  6. Write "not yet asked" with a date when a required answer is not known. Ask at the next contact with the family.
  7. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  8. Columns H, N, R, X, Z, AH, AI, AJ and AK hold dated entries. Add each new entry underneath the last one. Column AL holds one date, replaced at each check.
  9. The family's own words stay in the forms (FRM-ECS-02, FRM-ECS-03, FRM-ECS-05). This register holds dates, names, counts, record numbers and one-line pointers. Where a short phrase of the family's is entered, such as "none wanted" in column N, it is entered as it was said, signed or shown. Nobody tidies it.
  10. Column J takes record numbers only. Never write what was seen, said or suspected in this register.
  11. When the plan lead is away for more than 5 business days, the Service Manager names another worker to keep the row.
  12. When the system is down, complete the paper forms. Enter the row within 1 business day of the system coming back.
  13. A sole trader is the plan lead and keeps every row.

A row is closed only when all of these are true:

  • column AD is filled and column AC says "exited"
  • the family has their final progress report and their copy of the last plan
  • column AA shows the handover was given, or the family's decision that none was wanted
  • every consent line in column Q has a withdrawn date or an end date
  • nothing in column AE, AI, AJ, AK or AL is still due.

register.see:
• The plan lead and the key worker can see the rows of the children they work with.
  • The Service Manager, the Quality Manager and the Chief Executive can see every row.
  • A worker can see columns B, E, G, M, P, S, U and Y for the children they see. They cannot browse the register.
  • Column J shows record numbers only. Only the child safety lead, the deputy and the Chief Executive can open the forms behind those numbers.
  • A person with parental responsibility can ask to see their child's row and ask us to correct it. We answer within 10 business days (our standard).
  • Before a row is released, the child safety lead checks columns E and J. Nothing is released that an order forbids or that could put the child at risk.
  • Another provider in the team receives only what column Q allows.
  • An auditor or the NDIS Commission sees rows only as the law allows or requires.

Rows hold sensitive personal and health information about children. Keep the register in [system name], with a login for each person and a log of changes. Lock away any paper form.

POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets the wider privacy rules.
register.rows: The rows are the data. They are kept in the workbook or system built to this specification, not in this document. Where a cell would otherwise hold a list (columns E, H, I, M, N, P, Q, R, V, X, Z, AB, AH, AI, AJ and AK), a second sheet holds one row per entry, keyed to the child's record number in column A.
